core_job: For independent hosts of in-person events (supper clubs, fundraisers, DIY gigs, class socials) who take money themselves (cash at the door, Venmo, Zelle, Cash App): set up an event with its tiers, build the guest list (typed or pasted), run the door (codes, names, walk-ins, collecting what is owed), and end the night knowing who came, who paid and how, and whether the cash box balances. Everything stays on the device, with no account and no fees. The guest marketplace is removed. It is what puts "Live events coming soon" on the first screen today (search_failure.dart:44, inventory_source.dart:59), along with 3 hollow tabs and an invented catalogue.
signature: The Door Ledger. Each guest carries tier, party size, Paid/Owes/Comp, method and amount. Door mode checks a guest in and collects what they still owe in one tap, and sells walk-ins against each tier's remaining capacity, counting party size. Close-out reconciles the cash box (float + cash taken vs counted gives Over/Short/Balanced), totals by method and tier, lists no-shows and anyone still owing, and copies a text report or an RFC 4180 CSV to the clipboard. I checked 7 competitor listings through the keyless iTunes Search/Lookup API (web search is disabled here); I did not test the apps themselves. Eventbrite Organizer (368260521), Partiful (1662982304), Posh (1556928106) and Luma (1546150895) handle tiers and the door only for money on their own payment rail, with fees. Partiful only says "Drop your Venmo or CashApp for guests to chip in". Guest List Organizer (474032896), Guest Manager (1460267612) and Guestlist (1168724694) describe door check-in but no money tracking. None of the 7 listings describes off-platform payment tracking or cash-box reconciliation.
must: M1 One product, hosting: delete the guest marketplace and the TripNest scaffold. That means discover, search, nearby, saved, organiser, live, agenda, monetisation, guest tickets and details screens, plus the sample_catalogue, sample_extras, affiliate, supplier_client, inventory_source, search_failure, payments, conferencing, networking, coming_soon, skeletons and error_view files, and every comingSoon or InventoryMode flag. No dart-define may switch features on or off. Tests are removed only in the same commit as the code they cover, and each removal is listed.

M2 Core job end to end. Events get a host-relevant kind, a free-text address (the 15-city list goes) and locale currency. A tier editor enforces overall and per-tier capacity, counting party size. Tiers, payment, party size and close-out are persisted; today serialisation.dart:225-247 drops tiers. The guest list gets search, filter chips (tier, paid status, arrived), paste-from-clipboard import with a duplicate and capacity preview, and a copyable guest pass. Door codes get a per-event Random.secure salt; legacy events keep their old codes. The dead Published, Event reminders and Price alerts controls go.

M3 Door Ledger (signature). Each guest gets a payment record (paid/owes/comp, method, amount); 'Taken' counts paid money only. Door mode adds one-tap collect-and-check-in, partial party arrival, walk-in sales against tiers, and a 10-second undo. Close-out shows float vs counted cash (over/short), totals by method and tier, no-shows and anyone still owing. The report and CSV copy to the clipboard. No new native plugins.

M4 Depth: empty states in the app's own words, 'Run it again' for past events, event search with Upcoming/Past, a corrupt store kept under a .corrupt- key plus a one-time notice, nothing that needs the network, and past events whose ledger can still be viewed and exported.

M5 Own identity. 'Marquee' palette: seed plum 0xFF4A1942, amber 0xFFE8A33D, paper 0xFFFAF4EC, backstage 0xFF1B1418, ink 0xFF2A1F26, stamp green 0xFF2E7D5B, stamp red 0xFFA8322D. No other app or spec uses any of these hexes (grep), and the text pairs pass 4.5:1 (computed). Bundled OFL fonts Bricolage Grotesque, Figtree and Martian Mono (URLs return HTTP 200; no other app uses them). Ticket-stub card shape. A 'Next door' home with no feed. The 5-tab NavigationBar is replaced by a single stack, with Cupertino icons and transitions on iOS. One inline ad banner on Home only, and no tab-change interstitial.

M6 New icon (ticket stub with check stamp) drawn by a script in the EventSpark repo. The EventSpark row is deleted from generate_app_icons.py:68. New launch screen on plum; the storyboard shasum must no longer be 3f6a9b27. The Android splash matches.

M7 Own onboarding: host name, then 'How do guests pay you?', which sets the methods door mode offers; no permission prompts. Settings becomes Hosting / Appearance / Your events / Privacy (Privacy choices kept) / Help. The 'How we make money' screen, the Build row, Menu and Profile go.

M8 Honesty: a banned-phrase test (coming soon, this build, not available yet, not connected, sample, example, Simulator, ticketing partner, public catalogue). Every number comes from the host's own entries. No demo data, remote switches, reviewer detection or hidden gestures. The app never claims to process payments.

M9 Proven: flutter analyze clean and all tests pass (baseline is No issues found plus 536 passed). New tests cover ledger maths, tier capacity, the door widget flow, code uniqueness, legacy migration, persistence round-trip, paste import, CSV quoting, Run it again, banned phrases, theme tokens and fonts, and the shell. A screenshot integration test builds a real event. Simulator screenshots are attached. Commits are path-limited and pushed to main.
